releases.displayName: Mafia III: Definitive Edition Update Notes - Oct 22

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9765926/b807c845c534f1c96f37fe7789048302f8eef197.jpg"]

This new update for Mafia III: Definitive Edition addresses several issues reported by the community. We will continue to monitor feedback; thank you to everyone who has reported any issues and helped make the experience better for all players.
Updated the default Steam Input configuration for Steam Deck.
Updated UI element positioning on ultrawide screens.
Addressed multiple root causes of reported crashes.
Addressed various progression and functionality issues across multiple DLC missions.
Addressed a reported issue where disabling controller aim assist would have no effect.
Addressed several reported instances of instability during gameplay, including issues related to checkpoint loading and decompression.
Addressed various visual issues across DLC content, including incorrect lighting, floating assets, and vehicles despawning.
Fixed a missing waypoint during the “Follow Bouncer” objective in Sign of the Times.
Improved subtitles positioning when driving vehicles.
Improved UI scaling and display support for ultrawide monitor resolutions.
Improved localized text display, including Steam Overlay controls and initial language settings.
Improved animation reliability during select cutscenes and dialogue sequences.
Fixed a reported issue where controller input would not function on Steam Deck due to a non-functional community controller layout.

releases.displayName: Mafia III: Definitive Edition Steam Update Notes - Oct 8

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9765926/20f7eb108e935a9480e225c8ef7f05adaa260229.jpg"]

Family isn’t who you’re born with, it's who you die for. It's been 10 years since Mafia III made its debut on October 7, 2016, following Lincoln Clay as he blazes a violent path of revenge through the mob-run city of New Bordeaux in 1968. To celebrate, we're honoring a decade of Lincoln's legacy with a new Steam update bringing quality-of-life enhancements to Mafia III: Definitive Edition, live now.

Smoother mission progression: We addressed several spots where players reported getting stuck and unable to make progress in missions like "Get Enzo Conti," "Kill Tommy Marcano," and the Epilogue. No more dead ends when you're trying to finish the story. We also addressed reported crashes that could happen while driving into the Wharf, shooting a gas canister during "Destroy Boosted Car Shipment," or unlocking certain achievements mid-drive.
Improvements to Achievement tracking: Addressed reported issues with progress towards certain Achievements to ensure that your accomplishments are accurately tracked.

Better NPC and companion behavior: Characters like Alcee, Father James, and others didn't always behave as expected during missions, sometimes blocking your progress. We've cleaned up their behavior so missions flow the way they're meant to.
Improved mission progression and checkpoint reload behavior across several story missions.
Addressed a reported issue where previously completed objectives could remain marked as incomplete.
Addressed a reported issue preventing the district map from displaying correctly after certain objectives.
Addressed wiretap map data and junction box functionality loss after completing the Stones Unturned DLC.
Improved vehicle spawning behavior to prevent unintended collisions during specific objectives.
Addressed achievement progress loss if the game was closed mid-session.
Addressed various reported issues related to weapons and weapon upgrades
Addressed a reported issue causing the game to remain in slow motion after certain sequences.
Addressed several reported instances of instability, including issues during specific cutscenes, save loading, and combat scenarios.
Various additional improvements to mission scripting, AI behavior, and overall gameplay stability.
Addressed multiple instances of incorrect or flickering lighting in interior and exterior environments.
Addressed certain objects and environmental assets rendering with an unintended metallic or overexposed appearance.
Improved lighting draw distance for buildings, streetlights, and gas stations to reduce visible pop-in while driving.
Addressed unnatural square artifacts appearing during gameplay.
Addressed inconsistent shadow and lighting behavior on Lincoln and nearby NPCs.
Addressed various reported instances of missing audio, graphical artifacts, and unnatural animation found in cutscenes.
Added an option to toggle off game window borders.
Added new FPS lock options (120, 144, 180, 240).
Improved multi-monitor setup handling in windowed mode.
Addressed physics issues when playing in windowed mode with Vsync on.
Various improvements to visual fidelity and environmental stability.
Addressed several reported instances of missing or incorrectly placed waypoints during story objectives.
Corrected outdated and placeholder text appearing in specific UI elements.
Addressed subtitle settings resetting when launching the game.
Addressed a reported issue where the mouse cursor could move outside the game window when using multiple monitors.
Addressed various issues with crosshair functionality and visualization
Addressed debug texts appearing at the end of cinematics.
Improved consistency of UI feedback, including damage indicators, item icons, and upgrade confirmations.
Addressed various instances of missing or corrupted text in non-English languages
Various additional improvements to UI clarity and consistency across menus and HUD elements.

To everyone who stepped into Lincoln's boots over the last 10 years, or those who are just now seeing the sights and seedy underbelly of New Bordeaux for the first time, we're incredibly thankful for the support. We hope you enjoy the improvements made to Mafia III: Definitive Edition and its gritty rendition of the American south in the late '60s. If you're so inclined, take a seat at the table and discuss Lincoln's journey and the entirety of Mafia: The Omertà Collection with your fellow mafiosi by joining the official Mafia Discord.
We've pushed out an update that removes the 2K launcher.
Please see this 2K Support article for more details, as well as troubleshooting instructions: https://support.2k.com/hc/articles/34845053169939
● Miscellaneous bug fixes
Fixed issue: 2K Launcher fails to open on Steam Deck, preventing games from being launched.

releases.displayName: UPDATE: Mafia III Free Outfit DLC and New Patch Available Today

items.text: Lincoln Clay is ready to take on the mob in style – starting today, you can choose from 11 outfits while bringing down Sal Marcano. Along with Lincoln’s new threads, we’ve also rolled in a series of performance updates and hotfixes for Mafia III in a new patch. Keep reading for a breakdown of how the new outfits will work and what improvements are coming with the latest patch that is rolling out on all platforms now.
OUTFITS

This was a big request from you – our fans – so we made sure to get free Outfits to everyone that owns Mafia III, ASAP. So, suit up! With this update, you will now have 11 outfits to choose from: six outfits that Lincoln wears throughout different points in Mafia III’s story, and five all-new outfits. If you want to stalk the streets of New Bordeaux in military gear, you can. Want to get decked out like a proper Mob Don – no problem. Or maybe you just need a sweet racing jacket for when you tear through town in the Samson Drifter. Choose the best look for you!

As soon as you hit the “Somethin' I've Got To Do” mission, these outfits are available for you to pick your new look. Just head to your safehouse – or any racket hideout you’ve taken over – and head to the wardrobe. Ready for some killer style?
Action Gear: For all your combat wear needs.

UPDATE: PATCH NOTES

The dev team has also been hard at work addressing your feedback since the game launched on October 7. We’re happy to report that we’ve made a number of improvements on PC included in this patch. But we’re also not done improving the game, and will be making more updates to Mafia III in the future.
UI Improvements
Improved car reflections
Improved streaming issues
Performance optimization
Fixed audio issues
Fixed some cases of savegame corruption
Fixed various issues for Cassandra’s Contraband missions
And more

The work continues for the dev team as we still have more free content on the way – races and car customization! – and more updates for Mafia III. So keep an eye on our social channels for updates. And, most importantly, keep sharing your experiences with us. We want your stay in New Bordeaux to be an enjoyable one.

UPDATE 10/14: We just rolled out a hotfix on PC that addresses blurry rendering for some players, and other stability improvements.We’re still working on more fixes for Mafia III and will share more details in the coming week. Thanks for the feedback!
Original Post: Patch 1.01 Ready for Download

PC players, reboot Mafia III because patch 1.01 is now available for download. This patch includes 30, 60, and unlimited frames-per-second options on PC. To select your framerate, just head to the display menu in-game. Just make sure to tailor the framerate settings to the power of your machine. This patch also includes improvements to keyboard remapping, so head to the controls menu to check out the options. Note: this patch resets keyboard mapping to default, so any changes you made to the controls previously will need to be customized after installing the patch.

We aren’t done with fixes and updates and will continue to listen to our community for ways to improve your experience in New Bordeaux. And check here to see what content updates we have in the works, including outfit swapping, races, and more.
